pr_title: *: always convert sysvar values when out of range
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/25397

Problem Summary:

In MySQL sysvars that are of the correct type but out of range return a warning and not an error.

Previously TiDB returned an error unless `AutoConvertOutOfRange = true`. Now `AutoConvertOutOfRange = true` is permanently set, and the field has become meaningless and removed.

The error that TiDB returned was also not helpful (incorrect argument type).

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

When setting a system variable, TiDB now attempts to convert out of range values to the closest approximate value. For example, a value of 501 might be adjusted to the maximum value of 500. This behavior is more compatible with how MySQL accepts system variable values.

### Related changes

- None (not suitable for cherry pick)

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

Side effects

- Behavior change (but less strict, so unlikely to cause compatibility issues).

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- When setting a system variable, TiDB now attempts to convert out of range values to the closest approximate value. For example, a value of 501 might be adjusted to the maximum value of 500. This behavior is more compatible with how MySQL accepts system variable values.
pr_comments:
> Rest LGTM
> But should we consider this PR a compatibility breaker? Not every variable is `autoconvert=true` before, right?

I actually don't think it is compatibility breaking since it changes the server to be less strict (versus more strict; which usually is an issue). But it is easy to ague either way.

issue_context.title: Always convert out of range numeric sysvars to upper/lower bounds
issue_context.body:
## Development Task

In https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/25396 @dveeden noted that the error message for an out-of-range duration sysvar is not useful:

```sql
5.7.25-TiDB-v5.2.0-alpha-14-g75388187f 127.0.0.1:4000  SQL  set global tidb_gc_life_time='9m';
ERROR: 1232 (42000): Incorrect argument type to variable 'tidb_gc_life_time'
```

This is the same error with numeric types (TypeInt, TypeUnsigned) **unless** `AutoConvertOutOfRange = true`. I checked the behavior of various numeric sysvars (the ones that aren't enums) in MySQL and it seems like they always convert out of range:

```sql
mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > set global wait_timeout = 31537000;
Query OK, 0 rows affected, 1 warning (0.00 sec)

mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > show warnings;
+---------+------+----------------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                            |
+---------+------+----------------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1292 | Truncated incorrect wait_timeout value: '31537000' |
+---------+------+----------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > set global wait_timeout = -1;
Query OK, 0 rows affected, 1 warning (0.00 sec)

mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > show warnings;
+---------+------+----------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                      |
+---------+------+----------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1292 | Truncated incorrect wait_timeout value: '-1' |
+---------+------+----------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > set global bulk_insert_buffer_size   = -1;
Query OK, 0 rows affected, 1 warning (0.00 sec)

mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > show warnings;
+---------+------+---------------------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                                 |
+---------+------+---------------------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1292 | Truncated incorrect bulk_insert_buffer_size value: '-1' |
+---------+------+---------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > set global cte_max_recursion_depth  = 4294967296;
Query OK, 0 rows affected, 1 warning (0.00 sec)

mysql [localhost:8024] {msandbox} ((none)) > show warnings;
+---------+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                                         |
+---------+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1292 | Truncated incorrect cte_max_recursion_depth value: '4294967296' |
+---------+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

Should we just change all numeric sysvars to have this behavior and then remove the field for `AutoConvertOutOfRange`? This seems like it would match MySQL much closer.

One of the pre-requisites to this is making sure the range of Min/Max values is more accurate, but that should be the case in master already.
